title: Hearing the earliest bands and learning his first tune
summary: Barnes recalls hearing Buddy Bolden-era bands such as the Imperial and Superior, says he could play only one song then, and describes the hard Scott music.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I don't know whether I ever asked you whether you ever heard some of those very, very early bands, such as Bowling Band or any of those.
Well, in that time, Bowling Band, I wasn't playing.
No, no. You wouldn't remember if you'd have heard his band?

I did hear the band. Buddy Bowling, Marion Perez, and Nick Clark Crowe, and all that. And a bunch of them was different bands with the Imperial, the Superior, and Buddy Bowling, and what you called Jim Brown, all them. I remember that. But that was above my time. I wasn't playing. I was trying to play. You see, I was trying to play because I had but one song I played. Hey, what song was that really? That was the Got Good Bullies, so they say. What was that again?
Your Got Good Bullies, so they say.
Oh, that's right. You played that up at Tulane once, didn't you?
You played a little bit of it. Some of it there I tried to play.

Yeah, that one little tune, about a minute. I think we made a copy. That's when Herbie and Thomas and all of them were there that night. You played a little bit when they were between numbers. Yeah. Yeah, that's it.

Most of them times, the music was all Scott music, Top Jungle music. Scott Jepsen music. Yeah. It was hard music. It was like climbing, had a part in the day you'd make, and trombone and all that, and trombone. All that number, I wish I could remember them numbers. That's the Charles Hall, I don't know them. They all had the music. Gulong. Gulong.
